reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After freezing the final canonical and decision pair, rechecked the adopted regulations and exact catalogue entries before rereading the comparison. Recomputed the three 60 EC years, cross-checked the choice lists and exchange rules, and reconsidered the actual current workbook contributions before checking reader-facing fields.
findings: This is the English full-time standard BSc without formal named specialisations. Each of the first two years has eight required courses at 6.5 EC and two required skills at 4 EC. Third year contains 26 EC abroad, a 4 EC disciplinary skill selected from two options, two distinct 6.5 EC courses from a four-course list, a separate 6.5 EC approved elective and a 10.5 EC thesis. The current EER identifies the choices and the linked catalogues corroborate them. Optional menus remain open rather than representing earlier options as current or inventing routes. EER places Philosophy of Science in period two, whereas the OSP layout appears to put it in period one. The adopted regulations govern and the record does not assign an alternative period. All 180 EC are accounted for.

The nominal pathway completes all 60 first-year EC. The binding advice threshold is 47 EC with no named-course condition. The exchange requires 53.5 first-year EC at application and 60 before departure. Approved partner study contributes 26 EC and requires recognition, a transcript and study-abroad essay. Usual registration and attendance rules apply. Analysis I and linear algebra prepare for Analysis II, and probability for Mathematical Statistics. Optimisation and programming prepare for Operations Research, and the two project skills integrate the named methods already taught. Econometric Methods I is mandatory in semester four. Its catalogue gives introductory econometrics as expected background, with an example and separately specified exchange-student preparation. It does not identify a specific earlier passed module for the enrolled cohort, and the adopted nominal schedule contains no additional required module. No extra credit or earlier requirement is inferred. The two software skills use Econometric Methods I or Optimisation and Operations Research, respectively. The four disciplinary choices list preparation already present in the standard pathway. The 10.5 EC thesis is a supervised individual paper, ordinarily in semester six, with final paper and presentation listed as indicative assessment. The EER requires registration and adherence to the thesis guidelines. The public thesis entry lists no additional prerequisite. The nominal outline permits reversed thesis and exchange timing for delayed students.

Operations Research covers shortest paths, spanning trees, network flows and queues. UCR Algorithms & Data Structures covers the first two, and Optimization Methods in AI covers linear programming. Both are material academic overlaps, while the specialised sequence remains distinct. Econometric Methods I includes regression and inference as well as time series, which the UCR workbook does not establish in its Econometrics course. The applied option’s banking and market research give a defensible finance and market focus. Each schedule uses current offerings with earlier formal prerequisites, and seven courses differ in each direction. Maastricht’s integrated projects and 10.5 EC individual thesis are separate from optional UCR independent research.
